limits: A valid receipt says each party’s key signed its own part and the parts chain. It does not say any party told the truth.

The carried keys are the parties’ only if the verifier already holds those key_ids from somewhere else. A receipt cannot vouch for its own keys. When two roles are signed by one key, one holder signed both.
The acceptance names who accepted. The signature proves the acceptor’s key signed the receipt, not that the person named did.
money none means no money is held or paid by this receipt.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a receipt that still verifies.
The checks prove only what they test. A passed record says the pinned commands exited 0 on that tree, not that the work is good.
A test that cannot fail is not detected by this record.

The checker ran them as recorded only as far as the verifier trusts the checker’s key. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued the record, and content_hash that it was not edited since; the carried key is the checker’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a record that still verifies.
A delivery says what the doer’s Tick recorded handing in, not that the work is right. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
cents marked reported came from the agent’s platform and were not measured.
It does not prove the order exists or that this delivery answers it; that is checked where a receipt binds the two.
The carried key is the doer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A delivery cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a delivery that still verifies.
A work order says what was asked, not that anything was done. The signature proves the holder of the carried key issued it, and content_hash that it was not edited since.
The carried key is the buyer’s only if the verifier already holds that key_id from somewhere else. A work order cannot vouch for its own key.
limits is not covered by the signature: someone who removes it leaves a work order that still verifies.
payment none means no money is held for this order.

WHAT HAPPENED (2026-10-28, release 0.5.263 by tick_release). The thesis verification after the release (scripts/claims-verdicts.mjs over the gate's claims.json) said 12 of 35 claims met and 23 not met, almost all "packages/runner/src/git-workspace.test.ts did not run on this tree" and the like, and the briefing shows those theses as NOT MET. The tests had passed: scripts/land-check-theses.mjs judges a test file by "the record kept for the file's current key" in TICK_CHECK_RESULTS, and the release gate points TICK_CHECK_RESULTS at a store of its own, packages/cli/src/machine-release.ts:120 `results: join(beside, 'release-results')` (C:\Users\Asus\.tick\release-results, 1,548 records), while every check and landing records into the machine's one store, FILE_RESULTS_FOLDER in packages/runner/src/verified-trees.ts:32 (20,025 records on Parsa-TUF). The release gate runs only the test files the change since the last release reaches, so a file it did not reach has no record in its own store under its current key, though a check recorded its pass under that very key. The two earlier releases that day read 10 of 35 the same way.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. A release task's gate reads and records test results in the machine's store: machine-release.ts gives `results` as FILE_RESULTS_FOLDER (import it from @tick-executor/runner, as packages/runner/src/land-check.ts and flaky-drafts.ts use it; if the cli cannot import it, say so and use the same folder by the same rule). A record is a file's result under its key, which names the file and everything it depends on, so a pass recorded under a file's current key by any check on this machine is that file's pass on this tree: the reuse every landing check already relies on ("passed already on this same tree"). The release's own reports folder (`release-reports`) stays as it is.
2. Nothing is deleted: the old release-results folder is left where it is; say in your result that a person may remove it.
3. Tests. packages/cli/src/machine-release.test.ts:127 expects `join('/data/tick', 'release-results')`: change that value in place to the shared folder. packages/runner/src/release-wiring.test.ts:68 passes its own results folder to the runner and is not this file's concern; leave it. A new test in packages/cli/src/machine-release-results.test.ts holds that a release source's results folder is the folder the landing checks use (compare with FILE_RESULTS_FOLDER itself, not a copied literal). Grep the whole tree's *.test.ts for "release-results" and for `results:` in release sources before you finish; every other assertion keeps passing. If another file must change, ask for it with tick_widen; never weaken or delete a test.

DONE WHEN. Tick's check passes on your commit (call tick_check; do not install, build or run suites in your copy).
